question_type: CPI-deflated (rebased to a named month = 100) average of a monthly debt series over five months

opus_path.decision: Series = 'Total Federal securities outstanding' (OFS-1 column; equals FD-1 'Amount outstanding > Total'), end-of-month Feb-Jun 1980 (all inside FY1980, so no fiscal/calendar clash); normalization = rebase CPI so Feb 1980 = 100 and divide: real_m = nominal_m * CPI_Feb / CPI_m; average of 5 real values, 2 decimals. Listed the CPI-series ambiguity (NSA vs SA, 1982-84 vs 1967 base) up front.

Found OFS-1 and FD-1 in the Aug 1980 issue; both give identical totals; noted OCR errors in the FD-1 public-debt sub-column that do not affect the Total column (components sum to total within rounding).
Vintage check over 1980_05..1981_12: values unrevised; only OCR noise in 1980_10/1980_11. Used 1980_08.
calc.py re-reads the cited cells from the corpus and asserts them before computing (after first fixing a wrong line citation).
Searched the corpus for monthly CPI (only an annual 1967=100 row in 1983_06); concluded CPI is external.
EXTERNAL KNOWLEDGE: BLS CPI-U NSA, 1982-84=100 (CUUR0000SA0), and cross-checked those values against the 1967=100 series via a constant base ratio.
real = nominal * CPI_Feb / CPI_m, mean of five, in a script; sensitivity runs for the 1967 base and the SA series.

Sanity: Feb real equals nominal; real average is ~2.5% below nominal, about half the Feb->Jun CPI rise; magnitude consistent with FY-end gross debt. Reviewer re-read cells and recomputed independently.
Two decimals, millions of Feb-1980 dollars.

right_arms_note: No arm was right. All three extracted the same (correct, vintage-stable) nominal cells as Opus. All three failed first on recalled CPI values, and each arm recalled a different wrong 1980 path. none and cards added formula errors on top (inverted ratio; no rebasing).
text_vs_mechanism: Text alone cannot fix this. The prompt arm had the correct deflation-direction example and the 'CPI is external / commit once / no identical loops' lessons, applied the formula correctly, and still failed purely on recalled CPI values (and looped ~44x despite the no-loop lesson). This needs a TOOL (vetted CPI reference data) plus a CHECK (base-month identity and real<=nominal direction) for the none and cards formula slips.
notes: (1) GLM's CPI recall is unreliable and unstable: three arms gave three different Feb-Jun 1980 paths, and the prompt arm produced three different lists within one episode ([17], [29]). (2) The prompt learner's later lesson L-cpi-index-values-external-pin-series (seen in later adapters, e.g. the 106 AGENTS.md) inferred from this failure that the reference 'implies a seasonally adjusted CPI path, inconsistent with every NSA reading'. That inference was built on GLM's wrong recalled NSA values; Opus reproduced the correct result with the NSA 1982-84=100 series. So a text learner that back-solves external constants from the actor's recalled data can write wrong lessons, which argues for grounding external constants in a tool rather than in learned text. (3) The prompt arm's ~44 identical-command loop happened while its adapter contained L-no-identical-command-loops, so a CONTROL-level loop breaker (block a command whose exact text has already run twice; force commit) is needed for efficiency, though here it would not have changed correctness. (4) Plan/code mismatch appeared in two arms (none at [43], cards at [34] vs [41]): the stated formula differed from the executed one. A reviewer pass that re-derives the formula from the question and compares it with the script would catch both.
